title: Foods highest in saturated fat

seo.title: Foods highest in saturated fat: ranking and serving sizes
seo.meta_description: Coconut oil, butter, animal fats, dark chocolate and aged cheese can be high in saturated fat. Compare per 100 g and real portions.
seo.search_intent: Identify foods concentrated in saturated fat and understand how much a typical serving contributes.

excerpt: Coconut oil is one of the most concentrated common sources at roughly 80–85 g of saturated fat per 100 g; butter, palm oil and animal fats are also high. But 100 g is not a realistic serving of cooking fat: one tablespoon of coconut oil provides about 11–12 g of saturated fat, while an ounce of cheddar provides roughly 5–6 g.
content_html:
A per-100-g ranking makes pure oils and fats dominate saturated-fat lists. That is mathematically correct and easy to misread: no one needs to eat 100 g of butter for its saturated fat to matter.

The more useful comparison shows both concentration and serving size.

Foods that concentrate saturated fat

FoodSaturated fat/100 gServingSaturated fat/serving
Coconut oil~82 g1 tbsp~11.5 g
Butter~51 g1 tbsp~7 g
Palm oil~49 g1 tbsp~7 g
Lard~39 g1 tbsp~5 g
Dark chocolate, 70–85%~24 g1 oz~6.8 g
Cheddar cheese~19 g1 oz~5.3 g
Heavy cream~19–23 g2 tbsp~5–7 g

A common surprise is coconut oil: despite being plant-derived, one tablespoon can provide more saturated fat than small servings of many animal foods.

Plant-based does not automatically mean unsaturated

Olive oil, avocado and many nuts are dominated by unsaturated fats. Coconut and palm are important exceptions with much higher proportions of saturated fat.

Classifying fat only as “animal” or “plant” therefore loses useful information.

Dark chocolate shows why the whole food still matters

Dark chocolate contains substantial saturated fat from cocoa butter. A 1-ounce portion can provide around 7 g of saturated fat and roughly 170 calories.

It also provides fiber and cocoa compounds. Those nutrients do not erase the saturated fat; they simply show why one nutrient cannot describe an entire food.

Aged cheese concentrates nutrients as water is removed

Hard and aged cheeses contain less water than milk or yogurt, concentrating protein, fat, calcium and sodium. Cheddar can contain about 19 g of saturated fat per 100 g, but an ounce provides closer to 5 g.

Comparing 100 g of cheese with 100 g of yogurt ignores how differently those foods are normally served.

What the 10% limit means

Dietary guidance generally recommends keeping saturated fat below 10% of total calories and replacing it with unsaturated fat. On a 2,000-calorie reference diet, 10% is 200 calories, or roughly 22 g of saturated fat.

That is a reference scale, not an individualized prescription. One tablespoon of coconut oil can supply roughly half of it.

Replacement matters more than simply removal

Replacing butter with olive oil shifts fat quality from more saturated toward more monounsaturated fat. Removing butter and replacing its calories with large amounts of refined sugar is a different nutritional change.

The practical rule

The most concentrated sources include coconut oil, butter, palm oil and lard, followed by fatty foods such as some chocolates, cheeses and cream. Always look at the serving and, importantly, what that fat is replacing in the diet.

faq.question: What food is highest in saturated fat?
faq.answer: Among common fats, coconut oil ranks very high at roughly 80–85 g of saturated fat per 100 g.

faq.question: Does coconut oil have more saturated fat than butter?
faq.answer: Yes. Coconut oil is around 82 g/100 g versus about 51 g/100 g in butter; per tablespoon that is roughly 11–12 g versus 7 g.

faq.question: How much saturated fat should be limited?
faq.answer: Dietary guidance generally recommends keeping saturated fat below 10% of total calories and replacing it with unsaturated fats.
